note: Private mutation/regression corpus for SwiftInferProperties — the inference engine dogfooding on itself (Chapter 30 §30.4.4). Three families: mutants in the IdempotenceWitnessDetector's own name-classifier; mutants that undo a name-only-position guard (a key-path component's or a member's name read as a test-local); and mutants that undo one piece of the construction-facts wiring (the scan dropping its table or re-parsing the trees it was built from, the getter path judging without it, the universe admitting test targets, a test-directory scan walking up, the universe rule's shared-spec amendments — the nested-package bound, the manifest reader, smallest-path dedup, strict UTF-8, the root found from the path as given, the String < build order — the scans that must build no table, the speculative snapshot's universe, the staleness probe's manifests, and the census replica going blind to the construction witness). Each is killed by its own code's unit tests, which pin both what it should and should not do. Run via `swift test --filter`. Not a scored benchmark.

mutants.label: drop `reset` from the exact-name set — a genuinely idempotent action is no longer recognized as a witness
add `increment` to the exact-name set — a non-idempotent action is falsely classified as an idempotence witness
drop the `set` prefix — `setX`-style assignments are no longer recognized as prefix-match witnesses
ReceiverConstructionHarvester's free-name check skips member names only — `\.name` reads as a test-local and `Sorter(by: \.name)` is never harvested
ReceiverConstructionHarvester's inliner rewrites key-path names — `let pageSize = 10` harvests `Pager(sortedBy: \.10, pageSize: 10)`
the Slicer's identifier collector records member and key-path names — `.map(\.id)` and `{ $0.id }` pull an unrelated `let id = 7` into the property region
LocalBindingResolver substitutes into a key-path name — `let id = makeID()` makes `\.makeID()`, a component whose declName slot holds a call
MinedTraceSelector counts every lowercase name as a test-local — `Feature.State(color: .red)` and `Feature.State(sort: \.name)` are dropped
MinedTraceSelector skips every member name, not only key-path and leading-dot ones — `Feature.State(items: Self.fixtureItems)` is kept, pasted into the verifier stub, and fails its build
MinedTraceSelector reads `Self` as a type — `Self.Fixture()` names the test suite and is kept for a stub where `Self` is the stub
LocalBindingResolver skips everything inside a key path — `\.[id]` keeps the unresolved local where its argument should be substituted
ReceiverConstructionHarvester's inliner skips everything inside a key path — `Sorter(by: \.[index])` keeps the test-local

the package scan builds its ConstructionFacts and hands the visitor the unconfigured oracle — the table is built and dropped on the way, and a sibling target's `let id = UUID()` no longer refutes its constructor
the scan re-parses every judged file instead of reusing the universe's tree — SEI types an assignment by node identity, so `reset` is refuted by another target's same-named `A`
the universe predicate stops rejecting `Tests` / `*Tests` directories — a test target's `struct Item { let id = UUID() }` refutes a production `make() -> Item`
a scan under `Tests/Fixtures/X` walks up to the enclosing package — whose rule drops the fixture's own files, so its types never reach its table
the census replica stops consulting SEI's construction witness — 0 verdicts move on Sources/, so verdictAgreesWithSoundPurity stays green while 2 re-witnessed rows are filed as ignorance

the getter path judges with a fresh unconfigured PurityInferrer — a computed property constructing a sibling target's UUID-minting `Item` reads pure; every fixture subject was a function, so this survived both halves of the suite

buildOrder sorts with localizedStandardCompare (case-insensitive, numeric) instead of String < — `a` before `B`, `F2` before `F10`, so SEI reports a different first witness and the two consumers' tables disagree
the nested-package bound is computed and ignored — an unrelated `Demo/` package's `Row` refutes the root's own `make(n:)`, which main advised pure
localPackageDependencies takes any member call's `path:` — a target's `.target(name:path:)` reads as a local package dependency
two spellings of one file keep whichever the walk met first — the build order and the first witness follow directory-listing order, not the paths
the universe parse reads leniently, detecting UTF-16 by its byte-order mark — a file no compiler reads refutes `make`
the root is found from the RESOLVED scanned path — a symlinked `Sources/Lib` is judged at its destination, without the real sibling target whose `Item` refutes `make`
forJudging builds a purity for a directory with no Swift file — an empty scan parses the whole universe (1.30 s / 379 MB against 0.03 s / 12 MB)
the declarations-only scan drops the directory-wide PreconditionHelperHop — a helper in one file no longer marks an initializer in another, and its typeDecls differ from the full scan's
the staleness probe stops watching the manifests that decide the nested-package bound — adding `.package(path:)` leaves the index fresh

the speculative snapshot copies only Package.swift and Sources/ — a refuting `Core/` target or `Examples/` namesake vetoes laws in the baseline and not in the copy, so an unrelated widening is credited with them
a computed `path:` in the closure includes no nested package rather than every one — doubt under-refutes, the direction the spec forbids
the closure follows the root's own path dependencies but not theirs — a package the root reaches through another is dropped, and its `Row` no longer refutes
the manifest reader joins a literal's source text instead of its value — `"Pack\u{61}ges/A"` names no package (amendment H)
any readable Package.swift is a manifest — a `struct Package` source file becomes a package boundary and drops its target's other files (amendment F)
a dangling link or a directory named Package.swift is an unreadable manifest — doubt lets an unrelated Demo in, and a directory becomes a root (amendment F)
a Package.swift that cannot be read is no manifest — its doubt is lost and its package's files become the root's (amendment F)
an Xcode project beside the root manifest bounds nothing extra — the local package only the app target links leaves the table (amendment G)
dependency paths compared as folded text, never resolved — a `/private/tmp` literal, a symlinked prefix or another letter case misses the compiled package (amendment H)
only an absolute literal is resolved — a relative one through a symlinked package directory never meets the walked package (amendment Q, the critic's s11)
the closure reads only manifests the walk found — it stops at a package under Tests/, a hidden or a pruned directory (amendment I)
a directory's Package@swift-*.swift is never read — its dependency and its doubt are lost (amendment O, the critic's s6v)
a target's `path:` reaches no nested package — the root's own target inside `Core/` leaves the table (amendment P, the critic's s7)
a nested package holding a judged file is bounded out like any other — its functions are judged without their own types (amendment J)
a purity covers every scan under its root — a value built for Sources/App judges Examples/ under a table without Demo (amendment J)
the manifest is parsed on the caller's stack — a 3,000-arm `else if` manifest SIGBUSes the test process (amendment K)
the scanned path is taken as typed — on a case-insensitive volume the rule turns case-sensitive and members are spelled after the typing (amendment L)
the walk skips an entry carrying UF_HIDDEN — a flagged file SwiftPM compiles leaves the table (amendment M)
a speculative snapshot reads every universe member with `try` — one dangling link outside Sources/ skips every candidate
a speculative snapshot that throws is left in the temporary directory
the universe is deduplicated before it is bounded — a link into an uncompiled package is lost with the spelling the bound drops
the build order sorts by path component instead of String < — `Sources/A-B/X.swift` and `Sources/A/X.swift` swap (amendment N)
the manifests a universe watches leave out Package@swift-*.swift — an edit to one cannot mark the index stale
the walk prunes Tests/ again — a nested package there is never recorded, so a target path into it reaches nothing, where SwiftProjectLint's walk finds it
a directory's Package@swift-*.swift is read only when its Package.swift is a manifest — SwiftProjectLint reads them whatever Package.swift is
a dependency on a directory holding no manifest is doubt — every nested package comes in (amendment I says it passes nothing on)
covers computes a universe even for the directory the purity was built for — a root walk and a closure parse per ask (round 3, fix 1)
covers computes another directory's universe on every ask, never remembering the answer (round 3, fix 1)
the walk reads every entry's attributes again — 20,000 snapshot files under Tests/ blow the 0.5 s budget (round 3, fix 2)
the tools-version comment must be the very first line — a manifest after a blank line is no package (amendment S(a))
the tools-version label is matched case-sensitively — `// Swift-Tools-Version:5.9` is no manifest, fx/blank's root is lost (amendment S(a))
a tools-version comment below other lines counts at any version — SwiftPM below 6.0 rejects it (amendment S(b))
a 6.0 tools-version comment below a header is ignored — a copyrighted manifest is no package (amendment S(b))
a target path reaches only a package that holds it — `path: "Packages"` reaches none of the packages it compiles (amendment T)
the root's empty location matches no prefix — a root target's `path: "."` reaches no nested package (amendment T′)
